stories.title: Karoline Leavitt to Depart as White House Press Secretary
stories.summary: Karoline Leavitt will step down from her role as White House press secretary at the end of the month, as announced by President Donald Trump. Leavitt described her decision as bittersweet, having recently returned to work after the birth of her second child. She is noted for being the youngest person to hold the position and will continue as a senior advisor following her departure.

stories.title: Putin Observes Naval Drills Before Controversial Visit to Disputed Kuril Islands
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin observed naval exercises off Sakhalin Island before making a controversial visit to the Kuril Islands, which Japan claims. This visit has prompted strong protests from Japan, with officials labeling it 'unacceptable' and summoning the Russian ambassador to express their discontent. This marks the first visit by a Russian leader to the disputed islands since they were seized by the Soviet Union in 1945.

stories.title: UN Reports Highest Civilian Deaths in Ukraine Since May 2022
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that civilian casualties in Ukraine reached their highest level since May 2022, with at least 437 civilians killed and 2,610 injured in July. This surge in casualties coincided with an increase in long-range missile strikes by Russia. The data was provided by the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission.

stories.title: Rescue Operation Saves Woman Trapped for 36 Hours After Colombia Earthquake
stories.summary: Emergency workers in Colombia successfully rescued a 32-year-old woman who had been trapped for 36 hours under the rubble of a collapsed building following a powerful earthquake. The rescue operation took 10 hours after the woman was located beneath concrete debris in Pereira, as crews continue to search for additional survivors from the country's strongest earthquake in a century.

stories.title: Millions Experience Total Solar Eclipse Across Europe
stories.summary: On Wednesday, millions gathered across Europe to witness a total solar eclipse, the first of its kind in nearly 30 years. The eclipse's path of totality passed through parts of Greenland, Iceland, and northern Spain, creating a moment of awe as the moon completely obscured the sun. Many other regions, including the UK and France, experienced a partial eclipse, with over 90% of the sun covered in some areas.

stories.title: Congo's Ebola Outbreak Could Become Deadliest in History, WHO Warns
stories.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) has warned that the ongoing Ebola outbreak in Congo, declared on May 15, has already resulted in over 2,000 deaths and thousands of additional reported cases. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus indicated that if the current trend continues, this outbreak could surpass the deadliest Ebola outbreak recorded during the West African epidemic from 2014 to 2016.

stories.title: Colombia's Earthquake Rescue Operations Near Critical Conclusion
stories.summary: Rescue operations in Colombia are entering their final phase following a magnitude 7.4 earthquake that has resulted in at least 265 fatalities and left hundreds missing. As the critical 72-hour window for finding survivors approaches its end, rescuers are intensifying their efforts in collapsed buildings across western Colombia. The earthquake has displaced tens of thousands and caused significant destruction to infrastructure.

stories.title: Israeli Settlers Besiege Palestinian Families in Qusra, West Bank
stories.summary: In the West Bank village of Qusra, two Palestinian families have been besieged by Israeli settlers since Sunday, with reports indicating that they are cut off from water, electricity, and medical care. Israeli security forces have reportedly withdrawn from the area, leaving a group of settlers blocking access to the families' homes. The situation has drawn international condemnation, with a US diplomat labeling the actions of the settlers as an 'act of terror.'

stories.title: Putin's Visit to Disputed Kuril Islands Provokes Strong Reaction from Tokyo
stories.summary: Vladimir Putin visited the Kuril Islands, which are claimed by Japan, prompting an angry response from Tokyo. The islands, seized by Russia during World War II, are strategically important and rich in resources. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has publicly criticized Putin, particularly in light of Japan's sanctions against Russia due to the Ukraine conflict.
